subject: Differences between "unmarked" and R code in Kéry et al. 2005

messages.author: c35cde8d28a19782
messages.subject: Differences between "unmarked" and R code in Kéry et al. 2005
parts:
Hi everybody, I am a new unmarked-member and I would like to have your
advice.
A couple of years ago I analysed a dataset of repeated point counts of
different deer species, and I used the R code provided by Kéry et al.
(2005 Ecological Applications) with satisfactory results.
Now I am trying to analyse the same dataset with the unmarked package,
and I found an important difference in the results: when no
covariates are used, or covariates are used only to model abundance,
detection and lambda estimates are identical with the two methods, but
when covariates are added to model detectability the results of the
two methods diverge.

Has anybody used both methods and compared the results? I am pretty
sure this is my mistake, but I would like to be sure to use the right
code now (variables in the example are standardized, with zero-mean):

p3 <- pcount(~ hour ~ perc_open, datiUMF, K = 100)
lc1 <- linearComb(p3, c(1, 0), type="det")
backTransform(lc1)
lc2 <- linearComb(p3, c(1, 0), type="state")
backTransform(lc2)

Thank you in advance,

Simona Imperio, PhD
ISAC-CNR
Italian National Research Council
C.so Fiume 4, I-10133 Torino, Italy

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Differences between "unmarked" and R code in Kéry et al. 2005
parts:
Simona,
Its possible that the result is sensitive to K -- in fact, if there is a lot of over-dispersion or sparse data then sometimes the likelihood is unbounded at the boundary of the parameter space and there could be problems there that you should be careful of. You can try K=100, 200 etc.. and evaluate the sensitivity issue.
 
Other than that I can't think of a reason why results should differ.
 
regards,
andy
